title: Benchmarking Probabilistic Modeling Methods for Protein Fitness Prediction and Uncertainty Quantification
content: Accurately predicting protein fitness and quantifying associated uncertainties are critical challenges in protein engineering and drug discovery. This study benchmarks six advanced probabilistic modeling methods—Gaussian Process (GP), Bayes by Backprop (BBP), Deep Ensemble, Mean-Variance Estimation(MVE), MC Dropout, and Stochastic Weight Averaging-Gaussian(SWAG)—across eleven protein fitness datasets and a synthetic toy dataset. I evaluate these models under in-distribution (ID) and out-of-distribution (OOD) settings using metrics such as prediction accuracy, uncertainty estimation quality, and confidence interval coverage. The GP model demonstrates superior performance in prediction and uncertainty estimation across multiple datasets, particularly excelling in epistemic uncertainty evaluation. Ensemble models emerge as robust alternatives in OOD scenarios, effectively balancing prediction accuracy and uncertainty estimation. my findings underscore the importance of tailored data representations and metric selection in improving model performance. I advocate for standardized evaluation frameworks and explore future directions, including data efficient model training and the integration of uncertainty innexperimental design strategies like active learning. This work provides insights into the applicability of probabilistic models for advancing real-world protein engineering tasks.
